tldr: This thread is a loose grouping of arXiv papers on LLM multi-agent systems and agent policy training, not one developing story. Since Oct 25 it has collected work on learned and self-evolving orchestration, RL recipes for long-horizon agents, four agent benchmarks, and papers on auditing, privacy and failure attribution.
whats_new: Nov 13: AgentLeak, an open-source privacy-testing tool for multi-agent LLM systems, appeared as a Show HN, the thread's first item that is a tool rather than an arXiv paper.
why_it_matters: Multi-agent work is shifting from hand-wired workflows to learned orchestration, while tooling to audit, attribute failures in, and privacy-test those systems is only now appearing. Every result here is paper- or author-reported, not production evidence.

beats.headline: Papers move multi-agent design from one-shot wiring to learned, self-evolving orchestration
beats.summary: Self-evolution, coordination-aware prompt optimization, memory refinement, information-gap repair and learned orchestrators.

beats.headline: RL recipes for long-horizon agents target turn-level credit and partial verifiers
beats.summary: Multiscale and tree-structured policy optimization, a harness-as-policy analysis, open multi-agent RL axioms, and negative-only RLVR.

beats.headline: Four benchmarks test agents on robot control, security review, AI infra and workflow orchestration
beats.summary: EBench, Snyk VulnBench 2.0, Infrathon and WorkflowArena.

beats.headline: KV-cache quantization and small-model routing aim at multi-agent memory and compute cost
Auditing, private retrieval and failure attribution get proposed as multi-agent safety layers
Neighboring work: surveys, preference alignment, judge prompts, speech translation and flow models
AgentLeak brings open-source privacy testing for multi-agent systems to Show HN

open_questions: Does learned or self-evolving orchestration beat a fixed, hand-designed workflow on an independent benchmark such as WorkflowArena?
Does any independent group reproduce the turn-level or tree-structured policy optimization gains on long-horizon agents?
Does AgentLeak publish leak-rate results for named agent frameworks, and are they independently reproduced?
Does failure attribution like CoLFA identify the responsible agent and step accurately on production traces, not only on its own benchmarks?
Does coordinated KV-cache quantization hold task quality when agents run different base models?
take_for_builders: Keep hand-designed workflows as the baseline when trialing learned orchestration, and add inter-agent data-leak and per-agent failure-attribution checks to your eval suite before widening what agents share.
